learning_outcomes.text: Student knows and understands the basics of Python programming language.
Student knows and understands which Python tools can be used for selected applications in electrical engineering.

Student knows and understands how to use Python tools for selected applications in electrical engineering - digital signal processing and visualisation, - electrical circuits analysis, - artificial intelligence, machine and deep learning.
Student has ability to acquire a new knowledge
Student has ability to acquire a new knowledge.

syllabus_topics: Introduction to Python: Why Python?, environmental setup, run scripts, GitHub overview, use of documentation, basic syntax, variable types, basic operators, objects and data structures, strings, lists, tuples, dictionary.

Python methods and functions: Matplotlib library introduction – figures and axes creation, iterative figures, colormaps. File input/output, comparison operators, statements, conditionals and loops, linear algebra operations, statistics and random numbers, interpolation and fit.
Procedural programming in Python: Math and logic computations: selection, sorting, stack, queue etc.
Fundamentals of object-oriented programming in Python: OOP paradigms, attributes and class keyword, class object attributes and methods, function overloading, inheritance and polymorphism.

Digital signal processing and visualisation in Python part 1 – introduction: Introduction to NumPy/SciPy library, signals importing and pre-processing, harmonics and stochastic signals, signal processing tools, data visualisation.

Digital signal processing and visualisation in Python part 2 – selected applications: Fast Fourier transform (FFT) for spectral analysis, discrete cosine transform (DCT) for data compression, noise reduction and signal filtering.
Electrical circuits analysis in Python part 1 - introduction: Introduction to Pyspice library, electrical and electronics elements representation, creating electrical diagrams.
Electrical circuits analysis in Python part 2 – selected applications: Modelling and analysis of electrical diagrams.
Electrical power system analysis and modelling in Python part 1 - introduction: Introduction to Pypower/Pandapower library, power flow analysis, interfacing with OpenDSS.

Power system analysis and modelling in Python part 2 – selected applications: Analysis of a power systems, influence of non-linear and variable loads, influence of distributed generation, reactive power compensation.
Power system analysis and modelling in Python part 3 – project: Solution of typical issues in modern power systems, influence of distributed generation, power factor improvement etc.
Machine learning and deep learning in Python for electrical systems part 1 - Applications of Python artificial intelligence libraries.
Machine learning and deep learning in Python for electrical systems part 2 - data forecasting: Analysis of the operation of renewable energy sources using artificial intelligence methods.
Machine learning and deep learning in Python for electrical systems part 3 - system diagnosis: Analysis of the operation of a distributed power system using artificial intelligence methods.
assessment_rules: Final grade is the arithmetic mean of the project score (50%) and the total lab exercises score (50%). For laboratory classes, one unexcused absence is allowed, but the student must catch up to get a positive score. Excused absences are to be caught up through an additional date or fully documented student's own work.
